description:
Defk.UpgradeTest (test/upgrade_test.exs) is racy: mix ci / mix test occasionally reports 204-205/206. Pre-existing (reproduces on main@d90d09c before the defk-x15 CI epic); observed on main after the epic too.

REPRO
- mix test --repeat-until-failure 100  -> fails within a handful of shards (e.g. seed 395754: 2 failures in run 2 of the loop; also reproduced on d90d09c running test/upgrade_test.exs ALONE, so not a parallel-suite artifact).
- Plain re-runs are mostly green (10 clean in a row once), so it is a ~1-2% race, load-sensitive.

SYMPTOMS (the two tests fail together, same root)
1) test/upgrade_test.exs:121 "reloading the same library while a kernel is suspended"
   match (=) failed at start_suspended (line 72):
     expected %{frames_live: 1, promotions: 1}
     right   %{yields: 1533, frames_live: 0, promotions: 1}
   => the frame was NOT counted live at assert time.
2) test/upgrade_test.exs:100 "a kernel suspended across an upgrade finishes in the old library"
   refute :code.soft_purge(mod) got true (line 108)
   => no Erlang frame was on the suspended process stack, so purge succeeded.

ROOT CAUSE SKETCH
start_suspended (lines 65-74) does wait_until(yields > 0) then :erlang.suspend_process(pid). suspend_process only takes effect once the NIF reschedules itself, and where it lands is a race between two places:
- mid-C-chunk (the NIF is parked inside the C library): frames_live == 1, an Erlang frame may be absent => soft_purge succeeds (failure 2), the assert at :72 passes.
- at a BEAM yield (the NIF just returned to the Beam stub): frames_live == 0 (failure 1), the Erlang frame for mod.spin is on the process stack => soft_purge is blocked, assert at :72 fails.
The test asserts only the first branch but the run can land in either.

WHY THIS MATTERS (product question, not just test noise)
The upgrade contract ("a suspended kernel must finish in the library it started in") is exactly what these tests prove. If suspension can land at a point where soft_purge succeeds, then a real upgrade under that timing frees old code while a frame is suspended -- the resume path after start_suspended must be shown correct for BOTH landing points, and the test should exercise both rather than assume one.

NEXT STEP OPTIONS
(a) Make the suspension deterministic: suspend, then look at stats.().frames_live and proceed accordingly (the two landing points want different purge assertions); or have the kernel park itself at a known safepoint so the landing is unambiguous.
(b) Assert the actual contract (frame finishes in the old library) independent of the landing point, branching the soft_purge/refute on frames_live == 1.
(c) Consult the defk-nbl upgrade design before picking: the resume-through-purging path (failure 2 timing) may currently be a REAL bug (kernel resumes into purged code and crashes) or may be safe by construction (frame carries its library ref). Must establish which before "fixing" the test. Needs the runtime source (frame/Library interplay in the C runtime + resume path) -- defk-nbl context in docs/CONTEXT.md likely names the design.

RELATED
- I noticed and fixed while investigating the x15 CI: the x15.5 apply->direct change exposed a compile-time type warning in elixir_mode_test.exs:711 (committed 15d9179). Unrelated to this ticket but came out of the same "look at mix ci output" pass.
title: Defk.UpgradeTest suspend race makes mix ci flaky
